definition: A tower or chamber, usually part of a church, in which bells are hung.
origin: From Old French berfrei (a movable siege tower), from a Germanic compound related to bergen (to protect) and frid (peace), originally naming a wooden watchtower with no connection to bells at all. The spelling later shifted under the influence of bell, and by the late Middle Ages the word had settled into its present meaning: the tower that houses a church's bells.
